chunks: Ubay ibn Hisham al-Nashiri from Thabit from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who was pleased with his aunt's slave girl, fearing the sin and fearing that he would have unlawful intercourse with her. He freed all his slaves and swore by oaths that he would never touch her. Then his aunt died and he inherited the girl. Is there any blame on him if he has intercourse with her? He said: 'He only swore regarding the forbidden [act], and perhaps God would have mercy on him, so He caused her to be inherited by him because He knew of her chastity.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man inheriting a slave girl he previously swore not to have intercourse with?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal nuance of a vow (*yamin*) made to avoid sin regarding a slave girl. He rules that since the man swore specifically to avoid the act of intercourse and God, knowing his chastity, granted her to him as inheritance, there is no blame (*junah*) in him consummating the relationship, illustrating the principle that divine mercy can validate what might otherwise be restricted by specific vows or circumstances.
